lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Basin, 2148. Sand to the horizon, and standing out of it at intervals, the tops of racks, like fenceposts in a field nobody farms. The heat shimmer has been here since the cooling failed a century ago.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Something underneath is still drawing power. You can hear it in the ground if you crouch: the same note, steady, for longer than anyone alive.

lines.speaker: dax
lines.text: Ash Camp's two ridges that way. I learned to shoot on this ground, off a rock about six hundred metres north, when I was nine.

lines.speaker: dax
lines.text: Haven't been back. Wasn't a decision. You just stop going somewhere and then it's been twenty years.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There is a man on the north ridge, prone, with a rifle and a notebook. Sand has drifted up against his left side. He has been there long enough for that to happen, and he does not appear to have noticed you at all.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ridges are empty. Whoever used to watch this place went south the year the stronghold fell, and nobody replaced them, because there was nobody left to do the replacing.
